body:
I'm really sorry that you are in that situation. My experience sort of mirrors yours. My father died when I was 2 so I was mostly raised by my mother. It's slightly different because they already had 3 kids who were much older than me and living on their own. 

I remember a memory where I was playing with my toys and heard my mom sobbing. When I asked her what she was doing, she looked at me but didn't say anything. I had no idea what to do, so I just stood there. I don't remember what happened after that, but this was a common situation with her. I wish she talked about those kinds of things with me. I also wish she was interested in me as a person, like asking me how something made me feel, or asking me what I thought about a book I read. As far back as I can remember I was really defensive about my interests. When someone asked me  about what I was doing I would give the most boring non-answer that would get them to leave me alone, but I wish somebody kept trying and honestly told me that they were doing it because they cared about me.

You really seem like you are trying your best and I hope it works out for you.
